prs.title: feat: React Aria Sheet component
prs.author: devongovett
prs.body:
This adds a new `Sheet` component to react-aria-components. A Sheet is a swipeable overlay that slides in from the edge of the viewport. It supports snap points, stacking, gesture-synchronized animations, overscroll padding, and multiple placements and swipe directions.

It's implemented entirely with native browser scroll gestures, on top of CSS scroll snapping and view timelines, which means it runs at native 120fps without any JavaScript touch handling. Below is a diagram illustrating how it works:

Assuming `position="bottom"`:

* The outer-most scroll container is 200vh tall and hides its scrollbar. Only its top half is visible in the window viewport. This creates the swipable area.
* The "stage" is positioned in the bottom half of the scroll container. It is a flex container which positions its child (the sheet itself) on the edge of the viewport (e.g. bottom).
* When the sheet enters, we perform a `scrollTo({top: '100vh', behavior: 'smooth'})`. This create the entering animation.
* The backdrop and the sheet itself support `swipeAnimation`, which is a CSS animation synchronized with the swipe gesture. This uses CSS view-timeline, which tracks how much of an element is visible and uses this to drive a keyframe animation. The timeline ids are defined at the `html` element so that any element on the page can use them, and attached to the `SheetContent` element.
